# Comprehensive Introduction to Embodied Navigation Navigation

### Have you completed the basic tutorial and understood embodied navigation, but are still confused about how to apply it in practice? Have you reproduced cutting-edge code, but it is too complex, making it unclear about the specific algorithm implementation steps? Or are you unable to use large models and other algorithms due to a complicated environment, a large dataset, or a complex download process?

### In this course, the basic testing environment is strictly maintained. Each algorithm is isolated into a separate file, and is combined and called by the main function. Various modules can be freely replaced (by understanding their input and output). This makes it convenient for continued use in the future. Moreover, each module is largely independent of the environment, allowing it to be replaced with other simulation environments or even deployed in a real navigation environment. Additionally, using a zero-sample navigation approach, embodied navigation can be achieved without any fine-tuning.

### This course provides detailed explanations on everything from basic environment installation to obtaining and downloading model weights, as well as the explanation and integration of various algorithms. It takes just “half a day” to master all the algorithms from perception and decision-making to planning and control. You can refer to the algorithms in the course for both getting started with embodied navigation and further in-depth research. I hope this can offer you a little bit of help in your research and academic life. Let’s get started~

## 1. Start from setting up the environment

If you do not want to configure the environment, this course also provides image support. You can go to the following address on Autodl: https://www.autodl.art/i/datawhalechina/every-embodied/datawhale-navigation

The navigation README for the Autodl image contains detailed instructions for running the image. The gpu-free option also supports the image, allowing you to search for datawhale within the image and select the loading avatar navigation comprehensive introductory practice image.

### 1. Configure the conda environment

Create a navigation environment and activate it

```python
conda create -n navigation python=3.9 cmake=3.14.0
conda activate navigation
```

Install habitat-sim=0.2.5

```python
conda install habitat-sim=0.2.5 withbullet headless -c conda-forge -c aihabitat
```

## IV. Code Explanation

Most algorithms in embodied navigation are well-known, such as the YOLO visual algorithm, large language models, and planning algorithms. How to apply these algorithms to embodied navigation is what we need to explore and learn. This course aims mainly to help everyone understand and get familiar with the entire process of embodied navigation. It will explain the common pitfalls encountered during learning, providing some assistance for future research. That’s all I want~

Now, let's begin the detailed explanation of the algorithms. The discussion will focus on the integration of various navigation algorithms and the code sections that require additional learning for embodied navigation. For the principles of these algorithms, you can refer to other tutorials on datawhale, such as YOLO and large language model algorithms, which provide excellent explanations.

First, let me show you the overall VLM decision process for the code:

1) Rotational observation: 12 steps left turn, YOLO detection + 3D back projection + fog update

2) Deduplication and merging: Combine the 12-frame results, and select the highest confidence value for the same position and category.

3) Obtain the frontier points: Detect the frontiers, filter the visited frontier points, and select the top 8 based on distance.

4) Construct VLM input: organize detection summary, frontier summary, historical records, and key figures of 4 frames sampled.

5) VLM decision: Call the large model to parse JSON and output the decision.

6) Execute decision: Move the action toward the target object, front point, or random point.

7) Arrival judgment: If the distance is less than the distance for target detection, it is recorded as having found the target.

8) Termination check: Exit the loop when all targets are found or the number of steps is exhausted.

This is the complete process of a decision-making step in embodied navigation. I believe everyone has a preliminary understanding of the entire code. Next, we will provide a detailed explanation of each module in the code file.

### 1. config

```python
# ── YOLO ──────────────────────────────────────────────────
YOLO_MODEL = "yolov8n.pt"
YOLO_CONF_THRESHOLD = 0.35

# ── 本地 VLM (local 模式) ─────────────────────────────────
LOCAL_MODEL_NAME = "/home/robot/navigation/Qwen3-VL-4B-Instruct"
MODEL_DTYPE = "auto"
MODEL_DEVICE_MAP = "auto"
MODEL_MAX_NEW_TOKENS = 1024
MODEL_TEMPERATURE = 0.3
MODEL_TOP_P = 0.9
MODEL_TOP_K = 50

# ── 导航 ──────────────────────────────────────────────────
MAX_STEPS = 500
SPIN_STEPS = 12
VISIBLE_RADIUS = 3.0
MAP_RESOLUTION = 512
AREA_THRESHOLD_M2 = 9
TARGET_REACH_DIST = 1.5
```

In addition to some parameters in the previous configuration file, let's discuss the debugging basis for each parameter here.

1) YOLO_CONF_THRESHOLD: A value of 0.35 is an empirical value. If it is too low (0.1), shadows on the wall will also be detected as chairs; if it is too high (0.6), targets will be missed in dim lighting conditions.

2) TARGET_REACH_DIST is set to 1.5 meters. If it is too small (0.5m), the robot will hit the wall; if it is too large (3m), the VLM will misjudge that the robot has reached its destination.

3) MODEL_TEMPERATURE has a significant impact on decision quality. 0.3 is a more conservative choice, resulting in more stable output. When increased to above 0.8, the model may produce hallucinations, showing some objects that do not exist.

### 2. utils

1）simulator.py

This file is mainly used to create the habitat environment. If you have questions, you can refer to Chapter 8 [ in the [every-embodied] project ](https://github.com/datawhalechina/every-embodied/tree/main/08-%E5%85%B7%E8%BA%AB%E5%AF%BC%E8%88%AA%E5%8F%8AVLN), which provides a solid explanation.

2）geometry.py

```python
def depth_to_3d_world(depth_map: np.ndarray, bbox, agent_state, K: np.ndarray):
    x1, y1, x2, y2 = [int(v) for v in bbox]
    mx = max(1, (x2 - x1) // 4)
    my = max(1, (y2 - y1) // 4)
    region = depth_map[y1 + my:y2 - my, x1 + mx:x2 - mx]
    if region.size == 0:
        return None
    valid = region[region > 0]
    if valid.size == 0:
        return None
    d = float(np.median(valid))
    if d <= 0 or d > 10.0:
        return None

    cx_px = (x1 + x2) / 2.0
    cy_px = (y1 + y2) / 2.0
    fx, fy = K[0, 0], K[1, 1]
    cx_c, cy_c = K[0, 2], K[1, 2]

    point_cam = np.array([
        (cx_px - cx_c) * d / fx,
        -(cy_px - cy_c) * d / fy,
        -d,
        1.0,
    ])

    rot = agent_state.rotation
    q = np.array([rot.w, rot.x, rot.y, rot.z])
    R = quaternion_to_rotation_matrix(q)
    T = np.eye(4)
    T[:3, :3] = R
    T[:3, 3] = np.array(agent_state.position)
    return (T @ point_cam)[:3]
```

The `depth_to_3d_world` function primarily converts the detected pixels into world coordinates. Specifically, YOLO only provides image coordinates (pixel positions), while we need 3D world coordinates (where the robot is and where the object is). The depth map tells us the distance of each pixel, and combined with the camera intrinsic parameters, it allows the 2D detection box to be backprojected into 3D space. This process is called depth backprojection, which serves as a key link connecting visual perception and spatial navigation.

### 3. perception

The perception module is not described in detail. The code is simple; it uses YOLO for visual detection.

### 4. mapping

```python
def detect_frontiers(full_map: np.ndarray, explored_mask: np.ndarray,
                     min_area: int = 8):
    navigable = (full_map > 0).astype(np.uint8)
    explored = (explored_mask > 0).astype(np.uint8)
    unexplored_nav = (navigable & (1 - explored)).astype(np.uint8)

    border = cv2.morphologyEx(explored, cv2.MORPH_GRADIENT, np.ones((3, 3), np.uint8))
    frontier_mask = (border & unexplored_nav).astype(np.uint8)

    n, labels, stats, centroids = cv2.connectedComponentsWithStats(frontier_mask, 8)
    pts = []
    for i in range(1, n):
        if stats[i, cv2.CC_STAT_AREA] >= min_area:
            c = centroids[i]
            pts.append(np.array([int(c[1]), int(c[0])]))  # row, col
    return pts, frontier_mask
```

The most important aspect of mapping mapping is the front edge detection, which is also a module used in most navigation papers for unknown environments. However, the principle is not complicated.

```python
    border = cv2.morphologyEx(explored, cv2.MORPH_GRADIENT, np.ones((3, 3), np.uint8))
    frontier_mask = (border & unexplored_nav).astype(np.uint8)
```

These two lines of code identify the edge lines of the explored area. The edge lines and the unexplored traversable areas = the front line.

```python
    n, labels, stats, centroids = cv2.connectedComponentsWithStats(frontier_mask, 8)
```

Then, take the centroid of each independent front region, which is a front point. Isn't it simple~

### 5. vlm

Traditional navigation makes decisions based on rules (going to the nearest target, otherwise exploring the nearest frontier), while we use a multimodal large model to understand the scenario and make more intelligent decisions.

1）base_engine.py

The main function of base_engine.py is prompt construction, user text formatting, JSON parsing, rule downgrading, and logging. The same logic is used for both API and local deployment, which serves as the input shared by multimodal large models.

```python
    def _build_system_prompt(self) -> str:
        return f"""你是一个具身智能导航机器人的决策大脑。你的任务是在室内环境中找到以下全部目标物体: {self.targets}

你需要根据当前观察到的图像、YOLO检测结果（含物体3D坐标和距离）、可探索的前沿点，做出导航决策。

决策规则:
1. 如果检测到了目标物体且距离合理(< 8米), 优先导航到目标物体
2. 如果检测到多个目标物体, 选择最近的未访问目标
3. 如果没有检测到目标物体, 选择最优的前沿点进行探索
4. 选择前沿点时, 优先选择距离适中、朝向较大未探索区域的方向
5. 如果所有目标都已访问, 返回 "task_complete"

严格以以下JSON格式回复, 不要输出其他内容:
{{
    "thinking": "你的详细思考过程: 1)看到了什么 2)分析各选项 3)做出决策的理由",
    "action": "go_to_object" 或 "explore_frontier" 或 "task_complete",
    "target_index": 选择的目标在对应列表中的索引(从0开始),
    "confidence": 0到1之间的置信度
}}"""
```

The `system_prompt` mainly tells the large model who it is and which rules must be strictly followed. Specifically:

* Clear role: You are the decision-making brain of the embodied AI navigation robot

* Provide 5 clear decision rules, with priority from high to low

* Forced output format: strict JSON, to prevent the model from acting freely.

```python
    def _build_user_text(self, agent_pos, visited_targets,
                         detection_summary, frontier_info, nav_history) -> str:
        text = f"""## 第 {self.count} 次决策

### 当前状态
- Agent位置: [{agent_pos[0]:.2f}, {agent_pos[1]:.2f}, {agent_pos[2]:.2f}]
- 已访问目标: {visited_targets if visited_targets else '无'}
- 待寻找目标: {[t for t in self.targets if t not in visited_targets]}

### YOLO 检测结果 (原地旋转360°汇总)
"""
        if detection_summary:
            for i, d in enumerate(detection_summary):
                p = (f"[{d['world_pos'][0]:.2f}, {d['world_pos'][1]:.2f}, {d['world_pos'][2]:.2f}]"
                     if d.get("world_pos") else "未知")
                dist = f"{d['distance']:.2f}m" if d.get("distance") is not None else "未知"
                tag = "目标" if d["is_target"] else "非目标"
                text += f"  [{i}] {d['class']} (置信度:{d['confidence']:.2f}) 3D位置:{p} 距离:{dist} {tag}\n"
        else:
            text += "  当前旋转一圈未检测到任何物体\n"

        text += "\n### 可用前沿点\n"
        if frontier_info:
            for i, f in enumerate(frontier_info):
                text += (f"  [{i}] 位置:[{f['position'][0]:.2f}, {f['position'][1]:.2f}, "
                         f"{f['position'][2]:.2f}] 距离:{f['distance']:.2f}m\n")
        else:
            text += "  无可用前沿点\n"

        text += f"\n### 导航历史\n{nav_history}\n"
        return text
```

The `user_prompt` mainly contains the information fed to the large model, including:

1) Visual image: 4 key frames are evenly sampled during one rotation and compressed into JPEG base64.

2) Summary of test result text: category, confidence, 3D coordinates, distance, whether it is a target

3) Frontier point information: up to 8 candidate frontier points with their positions and distances

4) Navigation history: The last 5 decision records, allowing the model to know where it has been.

```python
def _fallback(self, dets, fronts, visited) -> dict:
    """VLM 调用失败时的规则降级策略。"""
    if dets:
        tgts = [d for d in dets if d["is_target"] and d["class"] not in visited
                and d.get("distance") is not None and d["distance"] < 8]
        if tgts:
            tgts.sort(key=lambda x: x["distance"])
            idx = dets.index(tgts[0])
            return {"action": "go_to_object", "target_index": idx,
                    "reasoning": f"[降级] 检测到 {tgts[0]['class']}", "confidence": 0.6}
    if fronts:
        return {"action": "explore_frontier", "target_index": 0,
                "reasoning": "[降级] 无目标, 探索前沿", "confidence": 0.3}
    return {"action": "explore_frontier", "target_index": 0,
            "reasoning": "[降级] 随机探索", "confidence": 0.1}
```

The last one is to ensure that there is a fallback code in case of network disruption or model failure during actual deployment, so the system can still operate normally.

### 6. planning

This part primarily uses the `habitat_sim.GreedyGeodesicFollower` from habitat-sim, and outputs the action execution. After reaching the target point, this can be modified according to the simulation environment. Users can also add and replace the planner, as well as the controller, to achieve better results.

### 7. output

This part is the visual content, which can also be modified by yourself.

If you don’t understand the interactions between the modules, you can also run and study using a single file directly. ## 5. Problems and Pursuits

I need to explain the issues in this embodied navigation framework to you all. It is not flawless, and I hope these problems can provide some ideas for your future research. It is my honor and the original intention of this course to help everyone.

The two main issues with the code are as follows:

1) False detection problem in the perception module:

<div style="display: flex; justify-content: space-between;">
  <img src="../../../13-其他前沿项目复现/具身导航综合入门实践/assets/yolov8.PNG" alt="Image 1" style="width: 48%; margin-right: 2%;">
  <img src="../../../13-其他前沿项目复现/具身导航综合入门实践/assets/yolo-world.PNG" alt="Image 2" style="width: 48%;">
</div>

In the results of running yolo as a single file, it can be seen that yolov8 has issues with false positives during detection. Some people say that using yolo-world open detection with self-defined rules should not cause problems. However, my actual testing shows that even with yolo-world open detection, the problem of false positives cannot be completely resolved. For objects that are not very common, detection still fails. Therefore, it is necessary to improve the perception module.

2) Problem of converting 2D to 3D:

When only executing the two objects, the chair and the couch, I found no major issues and it even worked perfectly. I was very happy at that time. This issue was discovered accidentally while trying to test it multiple times when the system tried to find the TV. Do you think I was very troubled at that moment? No! I was still happy when I discovered this problem~ After all, in research, being able to identify a problem means there is a need to solve it. In this way, I can make even a slight contribution in this field~

```python
============================================================
  📝 大模型完整思考过程
============================================================

--- 决策 #1 ---
  位置: [0.9390037655830383, -1.5215539932250977, -2.021697998046875]
  检测: 13 物体,  前沿: 1 个

  思考: 当前检测到多个目标物体，包括tv（距离4.56m）、couch（距离3.94m）和bed（非目标）。根据规则2，应选择最近的未访问目标。couch在3.94m处，tv在4.56m处，因此优先选择couch。前沿点距离2.86m，但目标优先级更高，故不选择探索。置信度基于检测结果，选择couch的置信度0.63较高。

  位置: [3.9896955490112305, -1.600250005722046, -0.521697998046875]

  位置: [3.0499484539031982, -1.600250005722046, 2.3973488807678223]
  检测: 14 物体,  前沿: 3 个
  动作: go_to_object
  置信: 0.85
  思考: 当前检测到多个椅子目标，且距离均在8米内，符合优先导航到目标物体的规则。已访问'couch'和'tv'，剩余目标为'chair'。检测到的椅子中，距离最近的是[12]，位置[4.61, -2.42, 3.64]，距离2.16米，置信度0.79，是当前最优选择。因此应导航到最近的未访问椅子。
为什么这个全是前往物体的思考过程，我看大模型也有前往前沿点的过程啊
```

Please take a look. Have you noticed that the large model always goes directly to the object without exploring new frontiers? My chair is clearly in another room, so how can it not explore new frontiers? Has it really grown into a super artificial intelligence? No! Look here.

<img src="../../../13-其他前沿项目复现/具身导航综合入门实践/assets/error1.png"/>

In this image, after the robot arrives near the couch, it discovers a TV hanging on the wall and navigates to its vicinity. The problem arises here: during the conversion from 2D to 3D coordinates, due to the thinness of the TV and its proximity to the wall, the algorithm incorrectly places the coordinates behind the wall. This is caused by the algorithm’s conversion error. As a result, the robot directly moves behind the wall, which is where the chair is located. You can refer to the following image.

<img src="../../../13-其他前沿项目复现/具身导航综合入门实践/assets/error2.png"/>

It can be seen that after the navigation to the room with the chair, due to it being attached to the wall, the system determined that the robot had reached near the tv. Thus, in the upper-left corner of the video, it was indicated that the tv was found, and the detection resumed. When the chair was also detected in this room, a large-scale decision-making process was initiated, resulting in only three issues related to go_to_object.

So how to solve it?

I recommend several articles with code for your reference, which will help you learn better.

1）[GaussNav: Gaussian Splatting for Visual Navigation](https://ieeexplore.ieee.org/abstract/document/10870413/)

Unit: University of Science and Technology of China

Project homepage: https://xiaohanlei.github.io/projects/GaussNav/

Code link: https://github.com/XiaohanLei/GaussNav

Solution approach: It mainly achieves object instance-level 3D positioning and navigation through 3DGS.

2）[Towards Physically Executable 3D Gaussian for Embodied Navigation](https://arxiv.org/abs/2510.21307)

Unit: Zhejiang University

Project homepage: https://sage-3d.github.io

Code link: https://github.com/Galery23/SAGE-3D_Official?tab=readme-ov-file

Solution approach: Create a 3DGS environment with semantic and physical alignment for VLN, providing executable 3D positioning and interaction for objects.

3）[EmbodiedSAM: Online Segment Any 3D Thing in Real Time](https://arxiv.org/abs/2408.11811)

Unit: Tsinghua University

Project homepage: https://xuxw98.github.io/ESAM/

Code link: https://github.com/xuxw98/ESAM?tab=readme-ov-file

Solution approach: Real-time online 3D instance segmentation, using SAM’s 2D Mask to convert to 3D point cloud Mask, providing 3D coordinates of objects for embodied navigation.

## VI. Stay Away from BUGs

May we all stay away from BUGs, and may everyone fix the bugs easily~

* BUG-1

```python
ImportError: libEGL.so.1: cannot open shared object file: No such file or directory
```

When encountering the BUG of libEGL.so.1, simply update and install the following libraries.

```python
apt update
apt install -y libegl1-mesa libegl1-mesa-dev libgl1-mesa-glx
```

* BUG-2

```python
GL::Context: cannot retrieve OpenGL version: GL::Renderer::Error::InvalidValue
```

When encountering the GL bug, you can avoid it by running the following code.

```python
export LD_PRELOAD=/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libGLX_nvidia.so.0:/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libGLdispatch.so.0
```

If you encounter any other BUGs, feel free to point them out~
